name: Agents & LLMs
oneLiner: A static base of 41 concepts on LLMs and agents, plus an essay on what changes in a layered system once you add an agent.
summary: Three files served statically: `index.html` fetches `concepts.json` and renders concept tiles, `architecture.html` is a separate essay, and the rest is the licence and `.nojekyll`. No build steps and no installed dependencies, so `git clone` plus `python3 -m http.server` is enough to run it. Content is entirely separated from presentation: adding a new short is one JSON object with the fields `id`, `title`, `kind`, `def`, `note`, `lang`, `code`, `videoUrl`, without touching the HTML. The most interesting engineering decision is treating view state as an address: the active category and the query land in the query string through `history.replaceState`, every tile has an anchor built from `id`, and a button copies the current address to the clipboard. That lets a pinned comment under a video link into exactly one concept or one filtered view, which is the whole reason this page exists. The second decision of the same kind is a syntax highlighter of its own for Python, JSON and reasoning traces, written on three regex functions instead of pulling in Prism. The thing is finished as a page and unfinished as a media project: none of the 41 `videoUrl` fields is filled in.
stack: Vanilla JavaScript (bez frameworka i bez bundlera)
CSS ze zmiennymi, motyw jasny/ciemny w localStorage
JSON as the only content source
Google Fonts (Space Grotesk, IBM Plex Sans, JetBrains Mono)
tests: No tests: across the 7 tracked files there is not a single test file, nor configuration for any runner.
ci: no CI. The `.github` directory does not exist, so nobody checks even whether `concepts.json` is valid JSON, and that is the one file meant to be edited regularly.

docs.label: README with the concepts.json entry format

components.name: Dependency-free syntax highlighter
components.description: Three functions that tokenise with a regex: `hlPython` (keywords, strings, numbers, comments, calls, types), `hlJson` telling a key from a value, and `hlTrace` for reasoning traces. Purely textual, with no reference to the domain, so they drop into any static page as a replacement for Prism or highlight.js.

components.name: Stan filtra w adresie
components.description: `restoreFromURL` and `syncURL` write the category and the query as `?kind=&q=` through `history.replaceState`, preserving the hash, and a button copies the current address with a fallback path onto `execCommand`. Depends only on the category map handed in from outside.

components.name: Baza wiedzy
components.description: Renders tiles from `concepts.json`, filters on a combined blob of title, definition, note and code with the hit highlighted, counts entries on the category chips, and handles the `/` shortcut into the search field. The `KINDS` categories, the channel branding and the `CONFIG` block are hard-wired, so without an extraction this is a single-project page.

components.name: The content source
components.description: 376 lines, 41 objects with eight fields each. All 10 entries carrying a Mermaid diagram sit in the `prod` category, from `harness-engineering` through to `observability-tracing`, so the most heavily drawn part of the material is operations rather than model theory.

components.name: Essay: from CRUD to agents
components.description: The argument is stratification rather than replacement: what moves into the agent, what survives unchanged, and where authorisation, versioning, {{term:determinizm}} and idempotency stop being enough. It ends with two migration options, tools in front of the API versus alongside the API, and links back into specific tiles in `index.html`.

overlaps.reason: The same brand and the same YouTube channel written into `CONFIG`. This repository is the content backing for the shorts series, not a separate thing.
The same set of concepts (tool use, RAG, {{term:mcp}}, checkpointing, evals, human-in-the-loop), only as a 40-word tile instead of a 20-page chapter.
The `workflow`, `executor-edge`, `handoff` and `orchestration-patterns` tiles describe exactly the surface that book writes out at length as {{term:maf|Microsoft Agent Framework}}.
The `evals` and `agent-trajectory-evals` tiles define the concepts that project actually measures. One is the glossary of the other.

product: No buyer, and no point pretending there is one. This is a distribution and credibility channel: a concept base wired to a shorts series, with anchors to paste into pinned comments, so the value is measured in traffic to the channel, not in revenue. The closest thing to sales material is `architecture.html`, because it reads like an opening to a conversation about migrating to agents, but the essay does not sell anything either. The whole construction has one precondition: the series has to start.
gaps: **None of the 41 `videoUrl` fields is filled in**, so the `▶ watch` link promised in the README appears on no tile at all. The knowledge base exists without the series it was meant to accompany.
The README links to a generic `https://www.youtube.com`, while `CONFIG` in `index.html` points at `@_dev_insight`. Two different channel addresses in a repository of seven files.
The README still instructs 'set channelUrl before you publish', although commit `944dccb` already did it. The instruction is out of date against its own code.
The `CONFIG` block is duplicated across both pages with a comment saying 'keep the two in sync' instead of one file loaded by both.
You cannot confirm from the repository that GitHub Pages is switched on: there is a `.nojekyll` and a paragraph in the README, but no deployment workflow and no production address recorded.
next: Add a minimal workflow validating `concepts.json`: that it parses, that `id` values are unique, that `kind` holds an allowed value, that `def` is non-empty. One file, ten minutes, and it closes the only real failure this page has.
Fix the channel link in the README to match the one in `CONFIG` and remove the out-of-date instruction about `channelUrl`.
Fill in `videoUrl` for the published shorts, or strike the promise of a `▶ watch` link from the README until the series starts.
Extract `CONFIG` into a single `config.js` loaded by both pages.
Pin Mermaid to a specific version with SRI or keep a copy locally, and record the actual Pages address in the README once deployment is switched on.
highlights: 41 concepts across five categories with 10 Mermaid diagrams rendered per tile, and all 10 belong to the `prod` category: it is agent operations that got the drawings, not model theory.
A syntax highlighter of its own for Python, JSON and reasoning traces, written from scratch. The only external runtime dependencies this page has are Mermaid and Google Fonts.

View state is fully linkable: category and query in the query string, an anchor per concept from the `id` field, a button copying the current address. Exactly the mechanism a pinned comment under a short requires.

The essay, at roughly 3,300 words, links to primary sources, including the {{term:mcp}} specification of 2026-07-28, MCP Apps and A2UI, and has a section of its own titled 'two claims that do not survive contact with reality'.

The essay states outright that earlier figures taken from secondary aggregators were removed, because they could not be traced back to a primary publication. A rare thing in a text meant to promote a channel.
risks: The page advertises itself as a 'companion to the shorts' and links to not one short. A reader will see an unkept promise before they see any content.
With no validation of `concepts.json`, one comma too many turns the whole page into a 'Couldn't load concepts.json' message. The failure is total, not partial.
Content about the agent ecosystem has fast {{term:drift}}: the entries on MCP, A2A and evals carry neither a date nor a version pin, so there is no way to see when they stop being true.
10 commits, the last of them on 2026-08-22. The point of the project depends entirely on the channel, so without the series this repository dies quietly.
headline: Page finished, series never started: 0 of 41 videoUrl fields filled
